newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases travel restrictions on Pakistanis.
newsitem.headline: India eases travel restrictions on Pakistanis.

text.p: India on Thursday announced an easing of restrictions on travel by Pakistanis in what Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral called a "major new unilateral step" ahead of bilateral talks next week.

"The measures that I announce today are designed to add to the goodwill between the peoples of the two countries," Gujral told parliament. "They are an emblem of our earnest desire to establish and maintain relations of friendship and cooperation with our neighbour Pakistan."
Gujral lauded Islamabad's recent decision to free 38 Indian children detained in Pakistan since 1994 when a fishing vessel on which they were travelling was seized by Pakistani authorities.
The foreign minister said that currently Pakistani nationals could enter India only on visitors' visas designed mainly for trips to meet close relations.

"In keeping with our policy to promote people-to-people relations, we have decided to permit Pakistani tourists to visit India in groups," he said. Young and elderly Pakistani visitors will no longer have to report their arrival to police, and visa fees for "senior Pakistanis" will be waived.

Gujral's statement evoked a sharp reaction from the rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party which forced the adjournment of the lower house of parliament, demanding the release of Indian soldiers in Pakistani jails.
